A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same GREATGRAMMA paper. Corresponding text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendix C.

before.justification: Section 5 and Table 1 report original measurements of preprocessing time and online token-masking overhead across three grammars and three tokenizers.

after.justification: The original timing experiments remain in Section 5 and Table 1. Section 6 additionally reports an unsuccessful attempt to run LLGUIDANCE on the evaluation grammars.

M1.justification: Appendix A, Algorithm 2 adds an initial-state EOS self-loop emitting $. EOS transitions from terminal-recognizing states already existed in v1. The token-spanner construction, parser preprocessing, and online masking procedure otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate simplified Go, Java, and Python grammars with Llama, Llama-3, and Qwen-2 tokenizers. JSONSchemaBench is newly discussed as a benchmark used by other work, not evaluated by this paper.

E2.justification: Section 6 newly reports attempting LLGUIDANCE v0.7.27 on the evaluation grammars, obtaining ParserTooComplex errors. This adds a failed comparator evaluation without timing measurements. OUTLINES, SYNCODE, and XGRAMMAR retain their previous participation and reported outcomes.

E3.justification: The timing protocol retains five manually constructed programs per grammar, identical prescribed token sequences across tools, preprocessing time, and average per-token masking overhead. No revised sampling, preprocessing, metric, or timing procedure is reported.

E4.justification: No ablation, sensitivity study, or robustness analysis is added. The Java lexical-ambiguity example remains. The new LLGUIDANCE failure report provides no diagnostic analysis, while proposed lexer and parser extensions are discussed without experimental testing.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same per-token averages and geometric-mean speedup summaries. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All Table 1 values and reported geometric-mean speedups are unchanged. Section 6 adds the qualitative finding that LLGUIDANCE v0.7.27 produces ParserTooComplex errors on the existing grammars; no new comparable timing improvement is demonstrated.

T1.justification: V1 contains automata definitions and stack-related propositions but no end-to-end correctness argument. V2 adds Appendix C with lexer/transducer equivalence, an inverse-table property, and completeness and soundness arguments. It also formalizes producible terminals, prefix languages, and additional assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same efficient token-spanner-based GCD contribution, 17.71x preprocessing speedup claim, and low online-overhead claim. The new proofs address existing correctness claims rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 expands the limitations discussion with the size cost of higher-lookahead lexers and restrictions on extending the algorithm to nondeterministic PDAs. It also acknowledges possible downstream quality degradation from constrained decoding and discusses compatibility with mitigation methods.

D1.justification: V2 specifies LLGUIDANCE v0.7.27 for the added failure report and names Floyd's reachability algorithm when explaining producible-terminal precomputation. Existing Python/LARK implementation disclosures remain; no new hardware information or release of the authors' code or data is reported.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of LLGUIDANCE, JSONSchemaBench, constrained generation's possible quality costs, and complementarity with CRANE and grammar-aligned decoding. It also adds Floyd and Knuth references. The existing positioning against SYNCODE, DOMINO, and XGRAMMAR remains.

P1.justification: V2 expands the token-spanner explanation in Section 3.2, reorganizes the stack-dependence discussion in Section 3.3, and adds acknowledgments and Appendix C. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 4 are revised to display EOS transitions, and Figure 3 moves to the other column. Text and algorithm placements reflow around the additions. Figure 1 and Table 1 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: V2 improves explanation, documents an EOS transition, and provides fuller limitations and comparator context. Appendix C makes correctness reasoning more inspectable, but Theorem C.8 invokes Lemma C.7's extra continuation-realizability assumption without explicitly including it in the theorem statement, limiting the claimed theoretical assurance. With the timing evidence unchanged, these support a qualified, limited overall improvement.
